title: Chapter 3 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of lists, text formatting, quotes, code display, and entities!

questions.question: Which tag pair creates a bulleted list?
questions.explanation: <ul> (unordered list) with <li> (list items) produces bullet points.

questions.question: How do you nest a second-level list correctly?
options: Place the new <ul> as a direct child of the outer <ul>
Place the new <ul> inside an <li> of the outer list
Use a <li> within a <li> without a <ul>
HTML does not support nested lists
questions.explanation: Nested lists must be inside a parent <li> element.

questions.question: What does the `reversed` attribute on an `<ol>` do?
questions.explanation: `reversed` makes an ordered list count downwards from the total number of items.

questions.question: In a description list, which tag represents the term being defined?
questions.explanation: <dt> (definition term) is the term; <dd> is the description.

questions.question: You can use the `type` attribute on `<ol>` to change numbering to Roman numerals.
questions.explanation: `type="I"` yields uppercase Roman numerals; `type="i"` lowercase.

questions.question: Which tag indicates strong importance and is typically bold?
questions.explanation: <strong> means strong importance; <b> is just visual bold.

questions.question: When should you use `<em>` instead of `<i>`?
options: When you want to convey stressed emphasis
When you want italic text for visual styling only
questions.explanation: <em> adds semantic stress; <i> is presentational italic.

questions.question: Which tag would you use to mark a deleted price in a sale announcement?
questions.explanation: <del> represents deleted text; it's semantic and renders with a strikethrough.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `<small>` tag?
options: To make text tiny for design
For side comments and fine print
questions.explanation: <small> is semantic for disclaimers, legal text, and side comments; not just reduced font size.

questions.question: How would you properly display H₂O using HTML?
questions.explanation: <sub> creates subscript, used for chemical formulas.

questions.question: Which tag automatically adds quotation marks around inline text?
questions.explanation: <q> inserts language‑appropriate quotation marks.

questions.question: What should the `<cite>` element be used for?
options: The title of a creative work
A citation of a website URL
questions.explanation: <cite> marks the title of a book, movie, painting, etc., not a person.

questions.question: The `<blockquote>` element is an inline element.
questions.explanation: <blockquote> is a block‑level element, usually indented.

questions.question: Which tag would you use to display computer code inline?
questions.explanation: <code> is for inline code snippets; <pre> is for block of preformatted text.

questions.question: What does the `<abbr>` element do?
options: It marks an abbreviation and provides a full form via `title`
questions.explanation: <abbr> with a title attribute shows the expansion on hover, aiding accessibility.

questions.question: Which HTML entity represents the ampersand character (&)?
questions.explanation: & renders as & on the page.

questions.question: To display the string `` as text on a web page, you must write it as ______.
questions.explanation: Replace < with < and > with > so the browser doesn't interpret it as an HTML tag.

questions.question: Which tag preserves all spaces and line breaks exactly as in the source code?
questions.explanation: <pre> stands for preformatted text; whitespace is honoured.

questions.question:
What is the correct use of the `
` tag?
options: To insert a line break within a paragraph
To create a new block element
questions.explanation: creates a single line break; don't use it for paragraph spacing.

questions.question: Which tag represents a thematic break (a horizontal rule)?
questions.explanation: <hr> is a void element that draws a horizontal line indicating a topic change.

questions.question: You can nest an ordered list inside an unordered list.
questions.explanation: Absolutely. Any type of list can be nested inside another list's <li>.

questions.question: Which entity would you use to display the copyright symbol?
questions.explanation: © renders as ©. (© also works, but © is the named entity.)
